doc: Cloud fraction with ITCZ shifts that float32 cannot hold exactly (3.7, -6.123456789, 11.987654321, 0.1 and 17.123456789 degrees: every other case uses shifts exactly representable in float32): the shift enters the fade and the ITCZ gaussian as a float64 (a Python float), so a port that rounds it to float32 moves the answer by up to 1.1e-8 (measured: 2.7 to 38 times the tolerance band for every shift but 0.1, whose float32 error is 1.5e-9 degrees), above the tolerance. Hadley edges 30 and 12.5 (inputs.hadley_deg), a 0.5 degree sweep. Output [i, j] is hadley[i], shift[j]. Float64: rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-12.
